title: all present

decision.evidence_type: two joint all-SKU inspections with reversed image/region orders and renamed region IDs

forward.prompt:
These are every image in one clothing SKU. Each VIEW contains an original photograph and a sheet of its SAM3 mask regions. Every mask has a UNIQUE ID beginning with R; IDs never repeat in another view.
Find every visually distinct garment that has visible pixels in an available mask in EVERY VIEW. The same garment may be shown alone, worn, from behind, as a fabric detail, or partly hidden under another layer. Use ALL views to establish identity. Do not require a small visible collar or undershirt strip to have the full garment silhouette. Match by fabric, construction, color and the context. A jacket and its undershirt remain separate garments even if the layers are sewn together. Similar colors alone are insufficient. A mask mixing different garments is not usable. Do not invent unseen pixels or new mask boundaries.
First describe which garments are present and which disappear, using the region IDs printed on the crops. Then output JSON: {"tracks":[{"garment":"description","regions":["R001", "R004", ...]}]}. This is only an output schema, not an answer. List only supplied region IDs and assign each ID to at most one track. A track must cover EVERY VIEW with at least one visible region. Extra fragments of the SAME garment in a view may share a track. Unlisted regions are removed. Keep repeated styling too, if present in every view. Do not select by the item for sale. If nothing is visibly supported everywhere, return an empty tracks list.
forward.raw:
In each of the three views, we are shown the same three garments: a pair of blue jeans, a pair of white jeans, and a silver metallic skirt. The garments are arranged differently in each view, but their visual characteristics — fabric, color, construction — remain consistent across all views.

We are given three views, each with three mask regions (R001–R003, R004–R006, R007–R009). Each mask region corresponds to one of the three garments, and the mapping is consistent across views:

- In **VIEW control_06_all_present_v0**, R001 = blue jeans, R002 = white jeans, R003 = silver skirt.
- In **VIEW control_06_all_present_v1**, R004 = blue jeans, R005 = white jeans, R006 = silver skirt.
- In **VIEW control_06_all_present_v2**, R007 = blue jeans, R008 = white jeans, R009 = silver skirt.

Each garment appears in every view, and each mask region corresponds to one garment without mixing or ambiguity. Therefore, we can assign each garment to a track using the corresponding region IDs from each view.

---

**Garment 1: Blue jeans**  
Appears in R001 (v0), R004 (v1), R007 (v2) — consistent denim fabric, back pockets, brown leather patch.

**Garment 2: White jeans**  
Appears in R002 (v0), R005 (v1), R008 (v2) — consistent light-wash denim, front button fly.

**Garment 3: Silver metallic skirt**  
Appears in R003 (v0), R006 (v1), R009 (v2) — consistent shiny silver fabric, elastic waistband, A-line silhouette.

All three garments are visible in every view, and each is uniquely represented by its corresponding region IDs.

---

```json
{
  "tracks": [
    {
      "garment": "blue jeans",
      "regions": ["R001", "R004", "R007"]
    },
    {
      "garment": "white jeans",
      "regions": ["R002", "R005", "R008"]
    },
    {
      "garment": "silver metallic skirt",
      "regions": ["R003", "R006", "R009"]
    }
  ]
}
```
